concept.name: Block space
concept.definition: Block space is the finite capacity of each block to include transactions, measured in gas (Ethereum) or bytes/weight (Bitcoin); it is the scarce resource that gas markets price.
concept.intuition: Each block is a truck with a fixed cargo hold leaving at fixed intervals — when more freight shows up than fits, shippers bid up the price of space.
concept.mechanics: Ethereum blocks target half the block gas limit (e.g. 15M of a 30M limit) and can expand to the limit under demand; the base fee rises or falls up to 12.5% per block to push usage back toward the target. Because each transaction consumes gas against this cap, demand for block space directly sets fee levels.
concept.failure_modes: Sustained congestion makes the chain unusable for low-value transactions and invites MEV bidding wars; raising the block limit trades decentralization for capacity by increasing node hardware requirements.
concept.misconceptions: Block space scarcity is a design choice, not an accident — unbounded blocks would centralize validation. High fees signal demand for space, not a broken fee mechanism.
concept.example: If an NFT mint fills blocks to the 30M gas limit for several blocks in a row, the base fee compounds upward by 12.5% per full block, and a simple transfer that cost 10 gwei can jump past 200 gwei within minutes.

citations.source: Ethereum.org developer docs - Gas and fees
